- A **sawtooth wave**, for instance, is composed of a **fundamental frequency** and a certain number of **harmonics**, which are ***multiples of the fundamental***.

<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->
## Signal: Spectrum {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {.content style="padding-left: -50px;"}
::: {style="font-size: 90%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- Any sound can be decomposed into a ***sum of sine waves***.
- A **sawtooth wave**, for instance, is composed of a **fundamental frequency** and a certain number of **harmonics**, which are ***multiples of the fundamental***.
- The "*waveform*" representation (**time-domain**) doesn't really help us when analyzing complex, **aperiodic** sounds.
:::
- While it's possible to analyze the *spectral contents* of an **analog** signal with **filter banks**, the resulting precision is rather *low*, and unpractical to use.
:::
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
::: {.content style="padding-left: 15%;"}
{{< waveform amplitude=25 waveform=sine frequency=1.0 >}}
:::
:::
::::

<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->
## Signal: Spectrum {auto-animate=true}
<!-- ----------------------------------------------------------------------- -->

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="50%" .add-space}
::: {.content style="padding-left: -50px;"}
::: {style="font-size: 85%;"}
::: {style="opacity: 0.5"}
- Any sound can be decomposed into a ***sum of sine waves***.
- A **sawtooth wave**, for instance, is composed of a **fundamental frequency** and a certain number of **harmonics**, which are ***multiples of the fundamental***.
- The "*waveform*" representation (**time-domain**) doesn't really help us when analyzing complex, **aperiodic** sounds.
- While it's possible to analyze the spectral contents of an analog signal with filter banks, the resulting precision is rather low, and unpractical to use.
:::
- **Frequency domain** on other hand allows us to decompose much more precisely a given sound into its *frequential components*, with a technique called ***Fast-Fourier-Transform*** (**FFT**).
:::
:::
:::

::: {.column width="44%"}
::: {style="font-size: 135%;"}
::: {.content style="padding-left: 15%;"}
{{< faust faust/examples/spectrum-1.dsp deploy=true >}}
:::
